assign.request: UX rethink pass on /imagine/team/ — five sentences before/after, try an alternative layout (3-column card is the brief's suggestion for this realm since it is one real working board with counters), verify persistence mark and Reset with ui-test, make it more visual, land with finish-task.
steps: read brief, minion-rules, realm card, approved-five, paging vocab
build 3-column card alternative, measure, keep or revert
verify persistence mark + Reset with ui-test
ui-test primary drag gesture, console check

log.msg: server at :8110 confirmed 200 on /imagine/ and /imagine/team/. usage: session 30%, weekly_all 15%, weekly_scoped 9%.

BEFORE five sentences logged. what: a drag-drop kanban board, 6 people/12 tasks/4 lanes. use: drag a task between lanes, or click a person to filter. goal: leave knowing who owns what and that dragging moves it. hard: 2/5 - intro sentence explains it but counters were a muted footnote easy to miss. better: pull the live counters out of the footnote into something you actually see, and stop the lanes stretching to armchair width at 3440.

before shots taken at 1280 and 3440, before any edit. measured (script eval): board is already width:fill from yesterday's fix - column right edge = viewport edge at both widths (100pct). At 3440 the 4 lanes stretch to ~640px each (measured via imagine-lane-body rects) - all whitespace around 2-3 word task titles. Page's own counters sit in one muted monospace line below the lanes.

picked the owner's 3-column card over the approved-five and the paging surface-change: team is exactly the shape the first nine reviewers said it wins on (research/generated) - a live centre with real numbers beside it, not a menu of children. Built public/imagine/team/team.css (new file, imagine.css is shared with /imagine/game/ so out of fence) and restructured board()'s content() in page.js: left = intro+baseline mark+who-filter+density toggle, centre = the lanes grid only, right = a bordered readouts card (tasks shown, pts per lane, the page's own live counters).

bug I made and fixed before measuring: first version set container-type on .imagine-board-card and tried to restyle that same class from inside its own @container query - silently did nothing (Page.css's own :has(>.rail) comment: a container query never matches its own container). Fixed by moving container-type to a new .imagine-board-wrap parent, one level up. Also first threshold (50em) mis-fired because em in a container query resolves against the CONTAINER's font-size, not root - measured card widths directly (817px at 1280, 2478px at 3440) and set a plain 1100px px threshold instead.

measured after: at 3440 lanes now ~410-460px each (was ~640px); readouts card visible with border instead of a footnote; card gaps are the normal 24px --gap-default, no new dead space (probed left/center/right rects directly). width used ~99pct (unchanged - board was already fill). own-content height ~489px (was ~515px est. from before screenshot) - shorter because intro/controls/readouts sit beside the lanes instead of stacked above/below. At 1280 the card collapses to one stacked column below the 1100px threshold: own-content height grew ~420px to ~820px, but it is real visible content (readouts card + 4 lanes stacked) not padding, still fits with no new scrollbar (860px available). Checked 400 and 1920 too: 400 pages one-at-a-time as before and stacks cleanly (2x2 lanes), 1920 stays 3-column. Zero console errors at every width. KEEPING the layout - both honest measured wins (lane width, readouts visibility) at near-zero width/dead-space cost.

ui-test proved the drag, not just imported it: dragged 'Draggable column seams' Queued->Landed with a real pointer sequence (down, 3 intermediate moves, up). Store committed {resize:"done"}, chip reappeared under Landed, baseline mark turned green 'Saved. Your lane changes...' with no reload. Then drove the full 2-press Reset (arm -> confirm): store cleared to null, page reloaded, mark disappeared (baseline state), task back in Queued. Also clicked a person in the roster: label updated to their name and the board filtered live (one selector-scoping issue in my own test plan hit the known duplicate-.imagine-lane trap from two board instances in the DOM - not a page defect, ui-test skill's own documented trap).

console clean at 1280 and 3440 (shot.mjs) and through every ui-test run (drag, reset, filter) - zero errors in all cases. Also spot-checked /imagine/team/ada/ (a nested board instance): renders correctly with the same 3-column card, filtered to her 2 tasks, no errors.

AFTER five sentences. what: a drag-drop kanban board for a 6-person team - 12 tasks in 4 lanes - laid out as controls+intro left, live board centre, readouts right. use: drag a task card to another lane to move it, or click a person on the far rail to see just their work. goal: leave knowing the board's real state - who owns what, how loaded each lane is - and that dragging is exactly how you rearrange it, no reading required. hard: 1/5 - the intro sentence and the three-region shape do all the explaining now. better: the green Saved mark could say what changed, not just that something did.

assign.outcome: **Built and kept the owner's 3-column card on `/imagine/team/`'s board** — controls+intro left, the live drag surface centre, readouts right, collapsing to one stacked column below an 1100px card width. Fixed the four lanes stretching to ~640px each at 3440 (now ~410-460px, a real kanban-card width) and promoted the page's own counters from a muted monospace footnote to a bordered readouts card. Verified — not just imported — the persistence mark and Reset with `ui-test`: dragging a task saves and turns the mark green (`Saved…`) with no reload, and a two-press Reset clears the store and restores the original seed. Zero console errors at 400/1280/1920/3440. Left: PROPOSED (0) — everything fit inside `team/`'s own fence (one new file, `team.css`; edits confined to `board()`'s `content()`).
